verses.text: Celebrate the Passover of the LORD your God in the month of Abib, because it was in the month of Abib that the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
Sacrifice an animal from your flock or herd as the Passover to the LORD your God, at the place the LORD will choose as the place where his name will live.

Do not eat it with bread made with yeast. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, the bread of suffering, because you left Egypt in a hurry. Do this so that all your life you will remember the day you left Egypt.
Let no yeast be found anywhere in your land for seven days. And do not let any of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day remain until morning.
You must not sacrifice the Passover in just any of the towns the LORD your God gives you.
Sacrifice it only at the place the LORD your God will choose as the place where his name will live. Do it in the evening, when the sun goes down, at the same time of day you left Egypt.
Roast it and eat it at the place the LORD your God will choose. Then in the morning go back to your tents.
For six days eat bread made without yeast. On the seventh day hold a special meeting for the LORD your God, and do no work.
Count seven weeks from the time you begin to cut the grain in the fields.
Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God by bringing a free will offering. Give in proportion to the blessings the LORD your God has given you.

Be glad in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose as the place where his name will live. Celebrate with your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, the Levites in your towns, and the foreigners, orphans, and widows living among you.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and be careful to obey these rules.
Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days, after you have gathered in the grain from your threshing floor and the juice from your winepress.
Be glad at your festival, you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows living in your towns.

For seven days celebrate the festival to the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose. For the LORD your God will bless all your harvest and all the work of your hands, and your joy will be complete.

Three times a year all your men must come before the LORD your God at the place he will choose: at the Festival of Bread Made Without Yeast, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Shelters. No one should come before the LORD empty-handed.
Each of you must bring a gift as you are able, in proportion to the blessings the LORD your God has given you.
Appoint judges and officials for each of your tribes in every town the LORD your God is giving you. They must judge the people fairly.
Do not twist justice or take sides. Do not accept a bribe, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of those who are innocent.
Follow justice and only justice, so that you may live and take over the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not set up any wooden Asherah pole beside the altar you build for the LORD your God,
and do not set up a holy stone pillar, because the LORD your God hates them.
